claims.text: A molybdenum interlayer between W and CuCrZr reduces thermal stresses.
A molybdenum interlayer between W and CuCrZr improves bonding strength under fusion-relevant conditions.
A 10–30 µm Mo interlayer is an appropriate thickness range for the proposed W/CuCrZr joint.
Thermal cycling up to approximately 700 °C is representative of fusion-reactor operation for this joint.
Mo has thermal-expansion properties intermediate between those of W and CuCrZr.
The Mo interlayer decreases the effective thermal-expansion mismatch between W and CuCrZr.
Decreasing the thermal-expansion mismatch reduces interfacial stress.
Reduced interfacial stress mitigates crack propagation under thermal shock.
Mo-interlayer joints will exhibit less interfacial cracking than directly bonded W-CuCrZr joints.
Mo-interlayer joints will have greater durability under repeated thermal cycling than directly bonded W-CuCrZr joints.
Mo-interlayer joints will have greater structural integrity under reactor-like thermal conditions.
Directly bonded W-CuCrZr joints are prone to interfacial cracking under repeated thermal loads.
Directly bonded W-CuCrZr joints are prone to bonding defects under repeated thermal loads.
The performance benefit of the Mo interlayer may be limited above 1000 °C.
The performance benefit of the Mo interlayer may be limited after extended exposure.
Very high temperatures or extended exposure could cause additional metallurgical changes such as interdiffusion.
The long-term behavior of the proposed joint under high neutron flux and extended service remains undetermined without further experiments.
